audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gave Yasuo 5 of 7 stages against a 57.59% Aurelion Sol winrate over 1337 games, and the layers disagreed at first item and two items (phases[5..6].side = Yasuo vs win[5..6] = Aurelion Sol).
audit.why: Yasuo owns levels 1-5 outright — Sweeping Blade off your own wave plus a two-stack Steel Tempest knockup ends any channel. Level 6 is a wash once Falling Star exists to stun the approach, and Aurelion Sol runs away with it from one item.
audit.corrected: Yasuo / Yasuo / Yasuo / Yasuo / Skill / Aurelion Sol / Aurelion Sol, proposed as matched full+content pairs.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level-6 and late spikes named 'Comet of Legend' and 'Starsurge', and gave no cooldown numbers.
audit.why: Neither ability exists on the current Aurelion Sol. Last Breath is 70/50/30s and Wind Wall is 25/23/21/19/17s — both numbers change how you plan a window.
audit.corrected: Spikes rebuilt on The Skies Descend, Stardust, Last Breath's 70s rank-1 cooldown and Wind Wall's real duration.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer repeatedly claims Wind Wall negates Aurelion Sol's poke — whys[1], spikes[0], early and wants.foe[1] all say so — while the full layer's own tldr says the opposite in capitals.
audit.why: Breath of Light is a channelled beam with no projectile flag in the kit; Wind Wall blocks projectiles. The full layer is right and the content layer shipped the contradiction to the same page. The real reasons Yasuo wins early are that any CC cancels the Q and W channels, that a two-stack Steel Tempest knockup provides exactly that CC, and that his passive shield absorbs the chip you land first.
audit.corrected: Content layer corrected to match the full layer; Wind Wall reframed as a problem for your team's projectiles, not your beam.

edits.after: Wind Wall does not block Breath of Light — the beam is not a projectile — but two Steel Tempest stacks knock you out of the channel anyway, and his passive shield eats whatever you did land.

edits.after: Last Breath is 70 seconds at rank 1 and blinks to any airborne target, so one Steel Tempest knockup deletes you — hold Falling Star to stun the approach rather than to open a trade.

edits.before: Fully stacked with Comet of Legend, your global execute and ranged burst outscale his flat crit-based damage entirely, and his all-in windows become predictable and easy to play around from range.
edits.after: Fully stacked with The Skies Descend, your drag-and-execute threat outscales his flat crit damage entirely, and a 30-second Last Breath still needs a knockup you can refuse to stand next to.

edits.before: Yasuo's mobility and Wind Wall let him close the gap on your ranged kit and completely negate your Starsurge poke, and once he lands a Steel Tempest knockup his all-in damage output punishes your lack of early burst, so you're forced to play very defensively and avoid overextending through the laning phase.
edits.after: Wind Wall does not block Breath of Light, but that hardly saves you: Sweeping Blade dashes off your own minions, two Steel Tempest stacks knock you out of the channel, and his passive shield absorbs the chip you did land — so play behind the wave and never start the beam inside 475 units of him.

edits.before: Level 6 makes this worse, not better — Last Breath gives him a follow-up dash off any airborne proc and resets his own combo chain, so a single successful engage can snowball into a kill before your own Comet of Legend has scaling stars to threaten him back, meaning you still need to respect his all-in windows closely.
edits.after: Level 6 makes this worse, not better — Last Breath blinks to any airborne target and holds the knockup, so one Steel Tempest chain converts into a kill before your Stardust curve threatens him back. Falling Star is the answer: 120 seconds at rank 1, spent to stun his approach, never to open a trade you cannot finish.

edits.before: Your first item finally gives you the range and kite tools to punish his gap-closes before he lands a combo, and Wind Wall stops being enough to fully neutralize your kit; by two items and full stacks your global execute threat and ranged burst clearly outscale his flat crit damage, turning his all-in from a real threat into a predictable, dodgeable cooldown.
edits.after: Your first item finally gives you the range and kite tools to punish his gap-closes before he lands a combo, and a 17-second Wind Wall covers less and less of the ground he needs; by two items and full Stardust your drag threat and beam burst clearly outscale his flat crit damage, turning his all-in from a real threat into a predictable, dodgeable cooldown.

edits.after: Carry by scaling honestly — Stardust is permanent, and a Yasuo who never lands a knockup is just a melee champion inside your black hole.

edits.after: Ahead, starve the dash: shove with E so his wave is thin, then W over and burn him — with nothing to Sweeping Blade off, he has to walk at you through beam range.

edits.after: Yasuo wins by dashing off your minions into a Steel Tempest knockup, then holding you airborne with Last Breath.

edits.before: Yasuo whiffs Wind Wall and the lane briefly belongs to you.

edits.before: That is Yasuo’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.

notes: The two layers shipped opposite answers on the headline mechanic: the full-layer tldr says in capitals that Wind Wall does NOT block Breath of Light, while the content layer said four separate times that it negates your poke. Corrected the content layer, since Riot's kit gives the Q a channel flag and no projectile flag. Separately: the kit file tags Astral Flight with terrain 'creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes', but Riot's description only says he flies OVER terrain — I did not assert any wall-creation anywhere. Fabricated names killed: 'Starsurge', 'Comet of Legend'.
